chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the deceased visiting his family. He said: 'Yes'. So I said, 'In how many visitations?' He said: '(Once) during the Friday, and (once) during the month, and (once) during the year, in accordance with his status'. So I said, 'In which image does he come over to them?' He said: 'In the image of a nice bird, falling upon their walls, and looking upon them. So if he sees them with goodness, he is happy; and if he sees them with evil and needy, he is with grief and gloom'.
ai.seo_question: How does the deceased visit their family after death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of *Ziyarat al-Mayyit* is expanded to include the deceased's active visitation of the living, a practice rooted in early Shia tradition that emphasizes the continued spiritual bond between the dead and their kin. The description of the deceased appearing as a 'delicate bird' (*tayr latif*) reflects the Shia understanding of the *Barzakh* as a realm where the soul retains a perceptible, albeit subtle, physical form capable of observation and emotional response to worldly events. This periodicity—Friday, monthly, and annually—mirrors the rhythm of Islamic devotional life, suggesting that the deceased's spiritual status determines the frequency of these visits.
